_comment: Search and scoring rules — copy this file to config.json and customize everything below for your own job search. config.json is gitignored, so your real targets/keywords never get pushed anywhere.

titles._exclude_notes: Titles here are hard-rejected — a listing never shows up at all. Use keywords.boost with a negative weight instead for titles you want to demote but not reject outright (e.g. {"senior": -3} so 'Senior X' still shows but ranks lower, since plenty of 'Senior' postings at smaller companies are really mid-level).
titles._include_needs_technical_signal_notes: Optional second, looser tier for titles that mean genuinely different things at different companies (classic case: 'Customer Success Manager' or 'Account Manager' — the same title covers everything from pure relationship/renewals work to a deeply technical post-sale role, depending on the employer). A match here only counts if a keywords.technical_signal term also appears in the title or description; title.include matches never need this extra check. Leave empty to disable.

keywords._boost_notes: Positive weights favor a listing; negative weights demote without rejecting. A keyword matched in the title counts more than the same keyword in the description — see matcher.py's TITLE_HIT vs DESCRIPTION_CAP if you want to change that balance.
keywords._technical_signal_notes: Only consulted for titles.include_needs_technical_signal matches — keep this narrower than keywords.boost. Generic B2B-SaaS words ('enterprise', 'cloud', 'saas') show up in almost any JD and won't discriminate; pick terms that actually signal hands-on technical work for your field (e.g. 'api', 'sql', 'itsm', 'active directory').
keywords._block_notes: Any listing matching one of these is rejected outright, regardless of score.

companies._exclude_notes: Company names to filter out entirely — e.g. companies whose hiring bar doesn't fit your background, or ones you're just not interested in. This mainly guards the RSS feeds, which carry companies of every size.

locations._notes: The location classifier (jobagent/locations.py) is US-focused today — city/state/country parsing assumes US addresses. It still won't reject listings from other countries if unknown_ok is true; it just won't structure their location as finely.
locations._local_cities_notes: Optional hard requirement: if this list is non-empty, a listing is rejected outright unless it's remote-eligible OR its parsed city matches one of these exactly (case-insensitive) — e.g. ["Dallas", "Fort Worth", "Plano"] for a Dallas-metro-or-remote search. Leave empty to disable (no city restriction, matching current behavior).

sources._greenhouse_notes: The board slug is the company name in a Greenhouse-hosted URL, e.g. https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/<slug>/jobs/...
sources._ashby_notes: Same idea as Greenhouse — the slug from https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/<slug>
sources._workday_notes: Add {"tenant": ..., "wd": N, "site": ...} parsed from a target company's Workday careers URL. jobagent/workday.py works with any tenant.
sources._smartrecruiters_notes: Identifier from https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/<Identifier>/... — case-sensitive, and it's the URL slug, not the company's display name.

role_families._notes: Used only by `find-hm` to pick department search keywords for the hiring-manager X-ray search. Optional — if omitted, cli.py falls back to a packaged default tuned for a presales/technical-account-management job search (see DEFAULT_ROLE_FAMILIES in jobagent/cli.py). Override with your own career-track taxonomy below.

resume_analysis._notes: Used by the `tailor` command / dashboard's Tailor button to flag high-value JD terms even when they appear only once. Optional — if omitted, resume.py falls back to a packaged default vocabulary tuned for presales/tech/cloud roles (see DEFAULT_VOCAB in jobagent/resume.py). Override with vocabulary for your own field (e.g. clinical terms for healthcare, GAAP/audit terms for finance).
